newsitem.title: ITALY: Afghanistan set for best harvest in 18 years -U.N..
newsitem.headline: Afghanistan set for best harvest in 18 years -U.N..

text.p: Afghanistan might produce its biggest cereal harvest for 18 years in 1997, but the war-torn country will still need emergency food aid to stave off hunger, United Nations agencies said on Tuesday.
The Rome-based World Food Programme (WFP) and Food and Agriculture Organistaion (FAO) said in a statement that Afghanistan's overall 1997 cereal harvest was forecast at 3.66 million tonnes.
"This would be 18 percent higher than the 1996 harvest of 3.1 million tonnes and the biggest since the outbreak of hostilities in 1978," the statement said.
But it added that continued fighting north of the capital Kabul between ruling Islamic Taleban militias and opposition forces might damage crop prospects.

"If the intensity of military activities increases or the conflict widens over the next few months, harvesting could be interrupted, and a reduction from this forecast is possible," the agencies said.
And even if the 1997 harvest meets expectations, Afghanistan will still need 170,000 tonnes of emergency aid to feed some 1.75 million people.
WFP, the U.N. agency which oversees the distribution of emergency food aid, said it would supply 140,000 tonnes of this total, with other non-government organisations providing the remainder.
